mainEntity.name: Does one mouse mean the attic insulation is contaminated?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A sighting or scratching sound is a reason to inspect, but it does not prove that droppings, urine, nesting material, or animal remains reached the insulation.

mainEntity.name: Can mouse-contaminated insulation be covered with new insulation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Covering it does not remove the contamination, debris, odor, or damaged material underneath. Once contamination is confirmed, Good Attic recommends removal and full remediation.

mainEntity.name: Should active mice be handled before attic restoration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A pest professional should address active mice before the attic is cleaned and rebuilt. Good Attic can coordinate that work when needed.

mainEntity.name: Can mice return after attic remediation?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can. Closing entry points and restoring the attic can reduce the chance of another problem, but mice may find a new opening later. Continued maintenance and pest monitoring still matter.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the attic contains vermiculite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Do not disturb suspected vermiculite like ordinary insulation. EPA advises homeowners to assume it may contain asbestos and involve a qualified asbestos professional when removal is necessary.
